Both root defaults.toml and src/local_ai_hub/defaults.toml parse with Python tomllib (native read-only check exit 0); bounded source slices 720-755 show same `[resilience]` section, and targeted git_status says src/local_ai_hub/defaults.toml is clean (req_93dad19b3640). The reported duplicate-key issue at this location is not present in current source; MCP Hub status is also online, but active installed config identity remains separate. Fresh search locates `_claim_embedding_gpu` in embeddings.py; bounded source slice at SHA c40c88cb8f55c8d92645477f776ef3fad79b9370c65c0187e6dc27232b41df9f lines 756-790 shows `store.reserve` and `store.renew` failure or caught OSError/ValueError collapse to `False`; encode maps that to the same `gpu_reserved` error. Therefore the observed RAG denial does not prove an external live owner; underlying cause may be reservation contention, invalid/missing generation, or storage error. A subsequent status read showed admission available, which does not reveal the root cause. Existing async_jobs.py patch remains the only targeted modified source file, unstaged (req_98784b88711d); diff SHA ff73b5a43c62a7e450f96203201fea9ed5752336f3a9c60072d72036547e138b. Laya states the patch is foreign to her and still no handoff; Laya thread turn completed with idle status at cursor revision 139. The active cross-vendor retrieval plan plan_ad8164af4995 has empty task list and explicitly says keep existing dirty work intact (req_c6259933644c). Our current task list shows only this Stability task; no active Agent OS owner for the patch was found. Do not infer authorship from absence of a lease/task. No changes were made to source this turn.
